messages:
maria: quick check — noticed `X-Customer` values (customer_id) leaking into our staging proxy raw_request logs for streaming endpoints. This is showing up in request headers and sometimes in prompt snippets when clients attach context. Can we decide: scrub to `<REDACTED>`, HMAC with tenant salt, or disallow logging altogether? Also need a quick OK to enable full-body capture in staging for a 2h debug window (restricted access) to reproduce a correlation issue.

jamal: agree we should avoid plaintext. HMAC with per-tenant secret is my preference — non-reversible and lets us correlate across services. Key stored in KMS, rotate on schedule.

sec-bot: policy reminder: PII (including tenant IDs classified as customer-identifiers) must not be stored in logs unless approved by security. If approved, retention <=24h and access must be audited.

kai: ops note: we can flip a staging flag to capture full bodies for a timeboxed window and push to an encrypted S3 bucket with server-side encryption + restricted IAM role `infra:dev-debug`. We can also add an audit entry and auto-delete after TTL.

maria: proposed minimal scrubbing pre-flag — proxy scrub rule: replace header value and scrub prompt emails/phones. Example config (nginx/lua):
```
if ngx.req.get_headers()["x-customer"] then
  ngx.req.set_header("x-customer", "<REDACTED>")
end
```
And quick prompt scrub (js):
```js
body.prompt = body.prompt.replace(/\b[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,6}\b/g, "<EMAIL>");
body.prompt = body.prompt.replace(/\b\+?\d[\d\s()-]{7,}\b/g, "<PHONE>");
```
This keeps logs useful but removes obvious PII.

jamal: small callout — if we HMAC the header we keep correlation but must ensure service-side verification uses same secret. Also HMAC(key, customer_id, date) to limit replay correlation across time.

maria: ask: can security approve 2h full-body capture in staging (only `infra:dev-debug` access), retention 3h, HMAC header enabled, and scrubbing pipeline applied before tiny-monitoring exports? Will open a ticket with scope.

sec-approver: approved with conditions — 1) window limited to 2h, start time to be declared in ticket, 2) storage TTL 3h (auto-delete), 3) access only via `infra:dev-debug` and only 3 named people listed in ticket, 4) KMS key for HMAC must be rotated within 7 days if used for live data, 5) audit event generated for who accessed bucket. Postmortem required summarizing findings and confirming no sensitive data was retained. :lock:

maria: thanks — I'll file the ticket and tag the three devs. I'll include the exact start time.

kai: I'll prepare the s3 IAM policy and the small automation to auto-delete and emit audit events.

jamal: rolling HMAC patch and a short test in staging. pinging when ready. :thumbsup:

maria: awesome — will coordinate and close the loop. :eyes:
